extracted.intended_audience: Researchers serving as peer reviewers for PLOS Genetics (and other PLOS journals)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for researchers performing peer review of manuscripts submitted to PLOS Genetics, covering reviewer suitability, conflicts, confidentiality, what to assess in manuscripts, and procedural policies (signing, timing, revisions, and report handling).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer suitability and consent
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept an invitation only if you have the knowledge, time and objectivity necessary to provide an unbiased assessment of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only accept assignments you can complete competently and on time. By agreeing to complete a review you also give permission to publish your review under a Creative Commons Attribution CC BY license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model — single-anonymized
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS Genetics practices single-anonymized peer review by default: you will know the authors’ names, but your name will not be shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your review will appear in the editorial decision letter read by authors and other reviewers; anonymity of reviewer is preserved unless you choose to sign.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signed peer review (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: You can choose to sign your name to your review when you submit it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you sign, the authors and other reviewers will see your name; if authors publish their peer review history your name will accompany your comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portable reviews between PLOS journals
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors transfer their manuscript to another PLOS journal, your review will accompany it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to have your review considered by editors at another PLOS journal and possibly be contacted for re-review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of peer review history
rubrics_metrics.description: If authors publish their peer review history, the editorial decision letter and your review may appear alongside the published article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your name will not be shown with the published review unless you chose to sign your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaring competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A competing interest is anything that interferes with or could be perceived as interfering with a thorough and objective assessment of a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common examples: recent/current collaboration with authors, direct competition or scientific conflict, or opportunity to profit. Do not accept assignment if you have a competing interest or cannot be objective. If unsure, contact the journal; if asked to review anyway, declare the interest when submitting your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Crediting co-reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: If you had help completing the review you must share your collaborator’s name with the journal when you submit the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter the name in the designated question ('Has this review been co-authored with a colleague?') or email the journal; do not include the collaborator’s name in the text of the review itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep manuscripts and correspondence confidential and do not share information about submissions with anyone else unless previously agreed with the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make use of material or take advantage of information gained through peer review; follow the PLOS Confidentiality Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewing a manuscript previously reviewed elsewhere
rubrics_metrics.description: If you reviewed the article at another journal, consider the manuscript as a new submission unless instructed otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscript may have been revised and PLOS Genetics’ criteria may differ; when submitting your review, inform the editor that you reviewed a previous version.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to complete your review within 14 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need more time, email the journal as soon as possible to request an extension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer credit (ORCID/Publons)
rubrics_metrics.description: Link your PLOS reviewer account to ORCID or Publons to receive credit for review activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up syncing to have reviewer activity posted to your ORCID profile; this confirms you completed a review but does not publish review content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall criteria for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to being ethically conducted and scientifically valid, research published in PLOS Genetics should fulfill each of the following criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are core acceptance standards reviewers should assess when making recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should be original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the claims and results represent new findings or approaches relative to existing literature.

rubrics_metrics.name: High importance to researchers in the field
rubrics_metrics.description: The manuscript should have high importance to researchers in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the significance and potential impact of the findings on the relevant research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broad interest to researchers in genetics and genomics
rubrics_metrics.description: The work should be of broad interest to researchers in genetics and genomics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether the manuscript will interest a wide subset of genetics/genomics researchers, not only a narrow specialist audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rigorous methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The study must employ rigorous methodology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine study design, controls, statistical analysis, and whether methods are appropriate and robust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial evidence for conclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: There should be substantial evidence supporting the paper’s conclusions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine if data and analyses are sufficient to justify the claims; identify missing evidence or overinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify main claims and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: State what the main claims of the paper are and how significant they are for the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a clear summary of central claims and evaluate their importance for the field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess novelty and reference contrary prior work
rubrics_metrics.description: Are these claims novel? If not, which published articles weaken the claims of originality of this one?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite specific prior work that reduces novelty or overlaps with the manuscript’s claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextualization in previous literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the claims properly placed in the context of the previous literature? Have the authors treated the literature fairly?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether relevant studies are cited and whether interpretation is balanced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of data and analyses
rubrics_metrics.description: Do the data and analyses fully support the claims? If not, what other evidence is required?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify gaps between claims and supporting evidence and specify additional analyses or experiments needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assessment of additional work
rubrics_metrics.description: Would additional work improve the paper? How much better would the paper be if this work were performed and how difficult would it be to do this work?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge the scope and feasibility of suggested additional experiments or analyses and whether they are required for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods warranting detailed protocols
rubrics_metrics.description: Do any particular methods used in the manuscript warrant publication as detailed protocols or algorithms as supporting information online?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a protocol is provided (e.g., for an RCT), check for important deviations and whether authors explain them adequately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data deposition and accession numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Are original data deposited in appropriate repositories and accession/version numbers provided for genes, proteins, mutants, diseases, etc.?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require data availability and explicit identifiers so others can access and verify data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformity to relevant reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the study conform to any relevant guidelines such as CONSORT, MIAME, QUORUM, STROBE, and the Fort Lauderdale agreement?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check adherence to discipline-specific reporting standards and request compliance if missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sufficiency of methodological details for reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Are details of the methodology sufficient to allow the experiments to be reproduced?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request missing experimental details, reagents, protocols, or code necessary for replication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Is any software created by the authors freely available?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage availability of code/software; if not available, request reasons or access arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manuscript organization and clarity for non-specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript well organized and written clearly enough to be accessible to non-specialists?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point out unclear sections or jargon; recommend editing or a professional science writer when appropriate and notify the journal office if recommending professional help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of standardized nomenclature and abbreviations
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the paper use standardized scientific nomenclature and abbreviations? If not, are these explained at first usage?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Require consistent, standard terminology and that abbreviations are defined on first use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct constructive comments to authors (not only confidential notes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Although confidential comments to the editors are respected, any remarks that might help to strengthen the paper should be directed to the authors themselves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place actionable, constructive feedback in the author-facing review; reserve confidential concerns for the editor-only section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Availability for re-review of revisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are often asked to evaluate revised manuscripts and authors’ responses; original reviewers are requested to be available for re-review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate willingness to re-review and respond to editor queries about revision adequacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editing and handling of reviewer reports policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Board members should not edit or delete reviewer reports; PLOS staff will not change reviewer comments intended for authors except in limited cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS may only alter reviewer text if language is inappropriate for professional communication or contains confidential information or information that poses a major risk. If editors have concerns they should notify PLOS staff before sending a decision letter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional language and confidentiality in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewer comments should be appropriate for professional communication and avoid disallowed confidential information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews may be edited or withheld from authors if language is inappropriate or contains confidential content that could incur major risk if conveyed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision-making and role of reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors make the final decision on whether to publish each submission based on reviewers’ comments, the PLOS Genetics criteria for publication, and their own assessment of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should provide clear, well-justified recommendations but understand editors weigh reviews, author responses, and other material; decisions are not strictly majority-rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling conflicting reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers disagree fundamentally, editors may share all reviews with reviewers and request additional comments to help reach a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to provide further clarification if asked; know that experts may legitimately disagree and editors synthesize input.
